reader.requirement: At --std 85 the n-th USING operand of CALL corresponds to the n-th USING operand of the called program's header, whatever the names. This holds for BY REFERENCE and BY CONTENT operands and for contained and separately compiled callees.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses 2002 CALL phrases (RETURNING, AS, BY VALUE, OMITTED) at 85; the positional adoption by LinkageFormal.Position is the same code at every edition

reader.edition-search: EmitCallMethod adopts __args[f.Position]; a grep found no edition test on the formal-position path.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the positional correspondence is identical. Only the allowed operand kinds differ (85 refuses BY VALUE and OMITTED).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f21_07 covers one call. The probes add swapped names, BY CONTENT mixed with BY REFERENCE, an ODO table operand, and a separately compiled callee with reversed group and elementary operands.

probes.printed: CALLEE A=BBBB B=AAAA P3=-00123.45 LT=T1T2 / CALLER A=2222 B=1111 NUM=-00123.45 / SEP X2=2222 X1-H=11 / CALLER2 A=2222 B=11QQ
probes.expected: positional: the caller's B binds to the callee's A, and BY CONTENT NUM is unchanged; the output is the same at --std 2023

probes.printed: COBOL0900: CALL BY VALUE and PROCEDURE DIVISION USING BY VALUE require COBOL-2002

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR10  (5.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10

reader.notes: The probe printed the same output at --std 85 and --std 2023; 2023 adds only the archaic-element warnings for EXIT PROGRAM.

refuter.evidence: Probe r6a_positional_alias.cob (--std 85). (1) A dynamic CALL PNAME (an identifier holding 'SUBP') USING WT-E (3) WT-E (1), with subscripted elementary operands in reverse order: the callee prints 'P1=T3 P2=T1', and afterwards WT=YYT2ZZ. Each position is bound to its own storage. (2) CALL 'SUBP' USING WA WA, one operand in two positions: MOVE 'ZZ' TO P1 is seen through P2 ('SUB AFTER MOVE P2=ZZ'), and afterwards WA=YY. Both positions refer to the caller's one item, which agrees with §1985:X.5.2.4 GR13 (cite.py OK). cite.py: OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR10  (5.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10.
